title: Physio-Control LIFEPAK 12 - Lead/ECG Cable Connection Errors
description: Guide for troubleshooting intermittent or faulty ECG lead connections on the LIFEPAK 12 defibrillator using external checks before assuming internal faults.

steps.title: Verify Lead Connection Orientation
steps.instructions: Ensure all ECG lead connectors are fully seated in their ports. Check that patient electrodes are attached in the correct positions. Why: Loose or misaligned connectors are the most common cause of lead errors.

steps.title: Inspect ECG Leads and Cables for Damage
steps.instructions: Look for cuts, kinks, exposed wires, or broken snaps/pins. Gently flex the cable while observing if the error appears. Why: Damaged cables can cause intermittent or false lead errors.

steps.title: Swap Leads or Cables
steps.instructions: Use a known-good ECG cable or set of leads. If the error clears, the original cable is likely defective.

steps.title: Check Connector Pins and Ports
steps.instructions: Inspect lead pins for corrosion, bent pins, or debris. Clean gently with isopropyl alcohol if dirty. Why: Corrosion or debris can block proper signal transmission.

steps.title: Power Cycle the Device
steps.instructions: Turn the LIFEPAK 12 off, wait 10–15 seconds, then power on. Observe if the lead error persists. Why: Some intermittent errors clear after a reset.

steps.title: Verify Patient Electrode Quality
steps.instructions: Check electrodes for expiration date, adhesive integrity, and gel quality. Replace with fresh electrodes if necessary. Why: Poor skin contact can simulate lead faults.

CCR.Complaint: LIFEPAK 12 shows ‘Lead Off’ alarms intermittently with patient connected.
CCR.Cause: ECG lead cable pins slightly bent; patient electrodes poorly adhered.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced ECG lead cable and applied fresh electrodes. Verified error cleared and ECG waveform stable.

helpfulDetails: Outlet tested: Yes
Cables swapped: Yes
Alarm behavior: Intermittent “Lead Off”
Indicator lights: ECG leads LED flashes red
Unusual sounds: None
Unusual heat or smell: None
Final device status: Operational, ready for patient use

title: Physio-Control LIFEPAK 12 - Battery Discharge / Poor Runtime
description: Troubleshooting guide for rapid battery discharge and reduced runtime in the LIFEPAK 12 MRx defibrillator.

steps.title: Check the Battery Charge Status
steps.instructions: Ensure the battery is seated correctly and locked into place. Verify the charge level via the device display. Reason: Improper seating can prevent full contact, causing false low-battery warnings.

steps.title: Inspect the Battery Physically
steps.instructions: Look for cracks, swelling, corrosion on contacts, or leaks. Reason: Physical damage can reduce capacity or create unsafe conditions.

steps.title: Test the Charger and Charging Cable
steps.instructions: Confirm the charger is plugged into a live outlet and indicator lights are normal. Swap the charger with a known-good unit if available. Reason: Faulty chargers or outlets are common causes of incomplete charging.

steps.title: Check for Accessory Draw
steps.instructions: Ensure no ECG/defibrillation leads, monitors, or other attachments are connected while charging. Reason: Connected accessories may draw power during charge, extending charging time and reducing effective runtime.

steps.title: Verify Environmental Conditions
steps.instructions: Charge and operate the device within the recommended temperature range (typically 15–30°C / 59–86°F). Reason: Extreme cold or heat can temporarily reduce battery performance.

steps.title: Perform a Device Self-Test
steps.instructions: Run a full self-test with the battery installed. Observe battery runtime estimate and any fault codes. Reason: Confirms whether the device recognizes the battery correctly and reports expected runtime.

steps.title: Swap with a Known-Good Battery
steps.instructions: Install a verified, fully charged battery and repeat self-test. Reason: Isolates whether the battery or the device electronics are the issue.

CCR.Complaint: Device battery drains too quickly; runtime less than 30 minutes on a full charge.
CCR.Cause: Battery seated correctly; charger, outlet, and environmental conditions verified; self-test confirms short runtime.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced with a verified battery; device sent for bench evaluation due to suspected internal battery degradation.

helpfulDetails: Outlet tested and verified
Charger tested or swapped
Battery contacts clean and undamaged
Device self-test runtime recorded
Final device status (removed from service if problem persists)

title: Physio-Control LIFEPAK 12 - Defibrillator Not Charging to Energy Level
description: Guide for troubleshooting LIFEPAK 12 devices that fail to reach selected defibrillation energy levels, focusing on external checks before internal repair.

steps.title: Verify Battery Condition
steps.instructions: Check that the battery is fully seated and properly locked in place. Confirm battery charge using the device’s battery indicator. Swap with a known good battery to rule out weak or defective battery. Reason: A weak battery may not supply enough current for full energy charge.

steps.title: Inspect Power Connections
steps.instructions: If on AC power, ensure the power cable is securely connected and outlet is live. Test outlet with a multimeter or another device. Reason: Insufficient power input can prevent full capacitor charge.

steps.title: Check Defibrillator Pads and Cables
steps.instructions: Ensure pads are correctly connected and not expired or damaged. Inspect ECG/defibrillation cables for visible breaks or wear. Reason: Open or shorted circuits may prevent safe charge completion.

steps.title: Attempt Charge with Minimal Configuration
steps.instructions: Remove patient cables and pads, leaving only the device and battery. Attempt to charge to the desired energy level. Reason: Isolates potential patient circuit issues.

steps.title: Observe Device Indicators and Error Messages
steps.instructions: Note any “Charge Failed,” “Low Energy,” or “Check Battery” messages. Record the behavior for work order documentation. Reason: Provides clues whether the issue is battery, capacitor, or internal electronics.

steps.title: Test with Another Device (if available)
steps.instructions: Attempt same charging procedure on a second LIFEPAK 12 using the same battery. Compare results to determine if the issue is with the battery or the device.

CCR.Complaint: Device will not charge to selected energy level; displays ‘Charge Failed’.
CCR.Cause: Battery tested good; cables and pads confirmed intact; issue persists with device only.
CCR.Resolution: Device removed from service, labeled Out of Service, sent to Physio-Control for repair.

helpfulDetails: Battery condition and voltage
Any indicator lights during attempted charge
Error messages displayed
Condition and expiration of pads and cables
Final device status: Out of Service

title: Physio-Control LIFEPAK 12 - Defibrillator Printer / Documentation Faults
description: Guide for troubleshooting printer and documentation issues on the LIFEPAK 12, focusing on external checks before internal repair.

steps.title: Verify Printer Power
steps.instructions: Ensure the printer module or integrated printer has power. Check any power switches or LEDs. Why: Without power, no printouts are possible.

steps.title: Check Paper Supply and Orientation
steps.instructions: Confirm there is paper in the printer tray or roll. Ensure it is installed correctly (not upside-down or jammed). Why: Improper paper loading is a common cause of print failures.

steps.title: Inspect Paper Path for Obstructions
steps.instructions: Remove any torn paper, debris, or foreign objects. Gently clean the paper feed path if needed. Why: Obstructions can prevent printing or cause misfeeds.

steps.title: Confirm Printer Connection / Module Seating
steps.instructions: Ensure the printer module is properly seated if removable. Check that all connectors and latches are secure. Why: Loose connections may prevent data transfer to the printer.

steps.title: Check Device Settings
steps.instructions: Verify print settings in the LIFEPAK 12 menu. Ensure event documentation printing is enabled. Why: Incorrect configuration may suppress printing.

steps.title: Test with a Known Good Paper Roll
steps.instructions: Swap the current paper with a fresh, compatible roll. Why: Paper type or quality issues can prevent clear printouts.

steps.title: Perform a Test Print / Self-Test
steps.instructions: Use the printer’s self-test function if available. Confirm if the printer prints independently of patient data. Why: Isolates printer hardware vs device software issues.

CCR.Complaint: Printer will not print ECG strips or event logs.
CCR.Cause: Paper loaded correctly, printer powered, connections verified, but print test failed.
CCR.Resolution: Device removed from service, labeled Out of Service, sent to Biomed for repair.

helpfulDetails: Printer LEDs (status indicators) observed
Paper type and orientation used
Any unusual sounds from printer
Last successful print timestamp
Error messages displayed on device screen

title: Physio-Control LIFEPAK 12 - Alarms Stuck or Muted
description: Guide for troubleshooting muted, stuck, or persistent alarms on the LIFEPAK 12 to ensure patient safety.

steps.title: Verify Alarm Volume Setting
steps.instructions: Check that the device’s alarm volume is set appropriately. Some devices have a dedicated volume knob or menu setting. Why: An accidental mute or low volume setting is the most common cause of inaudible alarms.

steps.title: Check the “Mute” or “Silence” Button
steps.instructions: Ensure the mute/silence button is not engaged. Press the button to cycle through audible alarm states. Why: Mute may have been activated by staff or accidentally held down.

steps.title: Inspect ECG / Lead Connections
steps.instructions: Ensure patient leads are securely connected. Some alarms remain “active” if leads are off or cables are damaged. Why: The device may continue generating alarm conditions due to poor signal detection.

steps.title: Verify Battery and Power Source
steps.instructions: Check the battery charge and AC power if available. Weak batteries can sometimes affect alarm operation. Why: Devices may disable or alter alarm behavior when power is low.

steps.title: Check for Software or Mode Settings
steps.instructions: Review current operating mode (e.g., monitor-only vs. defibrillator mode). Some modes reduce or suppress certain alarms. Why: Mode settings can change alarm priorities and thresholds.

steps.title: Power Cycle the Device
steps.instructions: Turn the device off, wait 10 seconds, and power back on. Observe if alarms reset and sound normally. Why: Temporary software or system glitches can cause stuck alarms.

CCR.Complaint: User reports that alarms are silent or persist without stopping.
CCR.Cause: Device alarm volume was muted and/or software glitch caused alarms to stick.
CCR.Resolution: Checked volume and mode settings, power cycled device; issue persisted. Device labeled Out of Service and sent for repair.

helpfulDetails: Battery charge status
Alarm volume and mute setting verified
Mode of operation (monitor, AED, or manual defibrillator)
Any observed alarm lights or persistent error indicators

title: Physio-Control LIFEPAK 15 - Touchscreen Unresponsiveness / Freezing
description: Guide for troubleshooting LIFEPAK 15 touchscreen that is unresponsive or freezes.

steps.title: Power Cycle the Device
steps.instructions: Turn the device off and remove the battery if accessible. Wait 30–60 seconds and reinsert the battery. Power the device back on. Why: A simple reboot can clear software glitches causing touchscreen unresponsiveness.

steps.title: Check Battery Charge Level
steps.instructions: Ensure the battery is fully charged and properly seated. Swap with a known-good battery if available. Why: Low voltage or poor battery contacts can cause intermittent touchscreen freezing.

steps.title: Inspect the Screen for Obstructions
steps.instructions: Clean the touchscreen with a soft, lint-free cloth. Remove any screen protectors or adhesives that may interfere. Why: Dirt, moisture, or debris can prevent accurate touch registration.

steps.title: Check for External Device Interference
steps.instructions: Remove USB drives, data cables, or other accessories temporarily. Power on and test touchscreen response. Why: Connected peripherals or damaged cables can affect touchscreen performance.

steps.title: Perform a Software Reset / Reboot
steps.instructions: If available, use the device’s system menu to perform a software reset. Ensure patient data is saved or exported before reset. Why: Freezing may be due to software hang, which a reset can resolve without hardware repair.

steps.title: Observe for Patterns
steps.instructions: Note if freezing occurs during specific functions (e.g., recording, alarm silencing, or menu navigation). Why: Patterns can help determine whether it’s software-related or touchscreen hardware degradation.

CCR.Complaint: Touchscreen unresponsive; cannot navigate menus or access patient data.
CCR.Cause: Observed touchscreen freezing regardless of battery swap or power cycle. No external obstructions or peripherals causing interference.
CCR.Resolution: Device removed from service, labeled Out of Service, and sent to Physio-Control for bench evaluation.

helpfulDetails: Battery voltage and type tested
Device uptime prior to freezing
Any connected peripherals at time of freezing
Screen cleanliness and inspection notes
Final device status: Out of Service

title: Physio-Control LIFEPAK 15 - Battery Low / Failure to Hold Charge
description: Guide for troubleshooting LIFEPAK 15 batteries that fail to hold charge or show unexpected low battery warnings.

steps.title: Verify battery type and seating
steps.instructions: Ensure the battery is the correct LIFEPAK 15-approved battery model. Remove and reseat the battery to confirm proper contact with terminals. Improper seating can prevent charging or give false low battery readings.

steps.title: Check the battery charge status
steps.instructions: Connect the device to its standard AC charger and observe the charging LED indicators. Allow at least 2–3 hours for a full charge if the battery was fully depleted.

steps.title: Test with a known good battery
steps.instructions: Swap in a battery with a verified charge. If the device functions normally, the original battery is likely at fault.

steps.title: Inspect battery and charger connections
steps.instructions: Check for debris, corrosion, or bent terminals on both the battery and the device charger port. Clean gently with a dry, lint-free cloth if needed.

steps.title: Confirm charger functionality
steps.instructions: Test the AC charger with another LIFEPAK 15 unit if available. Verify that the outlet is live using a calibrated outlet tester.

steps.title: Check environmental conditions
steps.instructions: Batteries may fail to charge properly if too hot (>40°C / 104°F) or cold (<10°C / 50°F). Move device to a room-temperature environment and retry charging.

steps.title: Observe battery behavior during device operation
steps.instructions: Power on the device and note any rapid drop in battery percentage or low battery warnings. Confirm whether runtime is significantly below the manufacturer’s expected duration.

CCR.Complaint: Battery reads low shortly after charging; device powers off prematurely.
CCR.Cause: Battery failed to maintain charge despite proper seating and full charging cycle.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced battery with known good battery; removed original battery from service and tagged for evaluation.

helpfulDetails: Outlet tested
Charger LED lights normal
Battery terminals clean, no corrosion
Device ran for expected duration with replacement battery
Original battery labeled Out of Service

title: Physio-Control LIFEPAK 15 - ECG Misreading / Flatline Despite Leads Attached
description: Guide to troubleshoot ECG misreadings or flatlines on the LIFEPAK 15 by checking leads, cables, electrodes, settings, and external interference before escalation.

steps.title: Verify Lead Placement
steps.instructions: Ensure all ECG leads are connected to the correct patient locations. Check for lead reversal or loose connections; even one loose lead can cause a flatline or misreading. Proper placement ensures accurate detection of cardiac signals.

steps.title: Inspect ECG Cables and Electrodes
steps.instructions: Examine cables for visible damage, kinks, or fraying. Replace electrodes if they are dried out or past expiration. Confirm good skin contact and electrode gel integrity. Damaged cables or poor electrode adhesion can prevent signal transmission.

steps.title: Check Device Settings
steps.instructions: Verify the LIFEPAK 15 is in the correct monitoring mode (e.g., 3-lead vs. 12-lead). Confirm gain/amplitude settings and filter options are appropriate for patient condition. Incorrect settings may suppress or distort ECG waveform.

steps.title: Power Cycle the Device
steps.instructions: Turn the defibrillator off and back on. Reconnect the leads after power-up. Temporary software glitches can interfere with signal display.

steps.title: Test with Known Good Leads or Simulator
steps.instructions: Connect a known working set of leads or an ECG simulator if available. If waveform appears correctly, original leads or electrodes may be faulty. Confirms whether the issue is device or accessory-related.

steps.title: Check for External Interference
steps.instructions: Remove the patient and device from potential EMI sources (large motors, cell phones, other medical equipment). Electromagnetic interference can create false flatlines or noisy signals.

CCR.Complaint: User reports LIFEPAK 15 shows flatline ECG despite leads attached.
CCR.Cause: Leads, electrodes, or cable integrity were suspect; improper placement or dried-out electrodes possible.
CCR.Resolution: Checked lead connections and placement; replaced electrodes and cables. Verified correct device settings and power cycled. Device functioned normally after external adjustments. If unresolved, device labeled Out of Service and sent for repair.

helpfulDetails: Leads used (brand, type)
Electrode expiration date
Cable condition (visual check)
Device mode (3-lead/12-lead)
Any alarms or indicator lights
Patient skin prep status

title: Physio-Control LIFEPAK 15 - Failed Self-Test on Power-Up
description: Guide to troubleshoot LIFEPAK 15 devices failing automated self-tests during power-on.

steps.title: Verify battery status
steps.instructions: Ensure the battery is fully seated and charged. A low or poorly seated battery can cause self-test failure. Why: LIFEPAK 15 self-tests check battery health and connection first.

steps.title: Inspect battery and device contacts
steps.instructions: Remove battery and inspect terminals for corrosion, dirt, or debris. Clean contacts with a dry, lint-free cloth. Reinstall battery and ensure a snug fit. Why: Poor connection may trigger system errors during self-test.

steps.title: Check charger and power source
steps.instructions: Confirm the device is connected to a known working charger or AC outlet. Test the outlet with another device to ensure proper voltage. Why: Self-test may fail if battery charge is insufficient or unstable.

steps.title: Remove external accessories
steps.instructions: Disconnect ECG leads, paddles, and other attachments. Power cycle device without accessories. Why: Faulty or shorted accessories can cause self-test errors.

steps.title: Observe error codes/messages
steps.instructions: Take note of any messages displayed during the self-test (e.g., “Battery Low,” “Hardware Fault,” “Sensor Error”). This helps identify whether the issue is battery, electronics, or accessory related.

steps.title: Power cycle the device
steps.instructions: Turn off, wait 30 seconds, then power back on. Why: Temporary glitches can sometimes be cleared with a simple reset.

steps.title: Try a known-good battery
steps.instructions: If available, insert a fully charged, verified battery. Repeat power-on self-test. Why: Confirms whether the battery is the root cause.

CCR.Complaint: LIFEPAK 15 fails self-test on power-up, displaying error messages immediately.
CCR.Cause: Observed fully seated battery, clean contacts, and no external accessory faults. Device still fails self-test. Likely internal hardware/firmware issue.
CCR.Resolution: Device removed from service, labeled Out of Service, and sent to authorized repair vendor for bench evaluation.

helpfulDetails: Battery voltage and model
Any error codes or messages displayed
Charger and outlet tested
Accessories disconnected
Final device status before sending for repair

title: Physio-Control LIFEPAK 15 - Charging Faults / Slow Charge
description: Guide for troubleshooting slow charging or charging errors on the LIFEPAK 15, emphasizing external checks and proper device handling.

steps.title: Verify Power Source
steps.instructions: Ensure the wall outlet or charging station is supplying correct voltage. Use a known working outlet if possible. Why: Inconsistent power can cause slow charging or failure.

steps.title: Check Charger Connection
steps.instructions: Inspect the charger cable for frays, cuts, or loose connections. Confirm the charger is properly seated on the LIFEPAK 15 battery or device. Why: Loose or damaged connections reduce current flow.

steps.title: Inspect Battery Condition
steps.instructions: Confirm battery is compatible and not past service life. Remove and reseat the battery to ensure proper contact. Why: Aging or improperly seated batteries charge slowly.

steps.title: Observe Device Indicators
steps.instructions: Check for error codes or LED status lights on the device and charger. Note any abnormal behavior during charging. Why: Indicators may help pinpoint whether the device or battery is at fault.

steps.title: Try a Known Good Battery
steps.instructions: Swap with a verified working battery if available. Why: Confirms whether the issue is battery-related or device-related.

steps.title: Test Alternate Charger (If Available)
steps.instructions: Use another compatible charger to rule out charger failure. Why: Chargers themselves can fail or underperform.

CCR.Complaint: User reported that the LIFEPAK 15 charges very slowly and sometimes displays a charging error.
CCR.Cause: Battery was seated loosely and charger connections were inconsistent; battery approaching end of service life.
CCR.Resolution: Reseated battery, confirmed charger functionality, replaced aging battery with tested unit. Device now charges within normal runtime.

helpfulDetails: Outlet tested and verified
Charger cable inspected for damage
Battery health status checked
Device indicator lights monitored
Any error codes recorded

title: Physio-Control LIFEPAK 20 / 20e - Printer or Event Recording Failure
description: Guide for troubleshooting printer or event recording failures on a LIFEPAK 20 / 20e defibrillator, emphasizing external checks before internal repair.

steps.title: Check Paper Supply
steps.instructions: Ensure the printer has paper installed correctly. Verify the paper type matches manufacturer specifications. A missing or incorrectly loaded paper roll is a common cause of printer failure.

steps.title: Inspect Printer Door and Latch
steps.instructions: Ensure the printer door is fully closed and latched. Many devices prevent printing if the printer is not properly seated.

steps.title: Check Printer Connections
steps.instructions: Verify the internal ribbon or cartridge (if present) is seated correctly. Inspect cables or connectors for damage or disconnection.

steps.title: Power Cycle the Device
steps.instructions: Turn the defibrillator off, wait 10–15 seconds, and turn it back on. Power cycling can reset the printer interface and clear minor software glitches.

steps.title: Verify Event Recording Settings
steps.instructions: Confirm that event recording is enabled in the device settings. Ensure proper ECG lead and pad connections, as missing input can prevent event capture.

steps.title: Test Print Function
steps.instructions: Use the device’s built-in self-test or 'print test' function. This isolates whether the issue is with the printer mechanism or with event recording itself.

steps.title: Check for Obstructions or Damage
steps.instructions: Inspect the printer path for debris, torn paper, or jammed mechanisms. Look for visible damage to the printer gears or rollers.

CCR.Complaint: Device did not print ECG after shock delivery; event record missing.
CCR.Cause: Printer paper was depleted and printer door not fully latched. Event recording enabled but no printout generated due to lack of paper and improper seating.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced printer paper, reseated printer door, ran print self-test successfully. Event recording verified functional.

helpfulDetails: Paper type and status
Printer self-test result
Any error messages or beeps
Condition of printer ribbon/cartridge
Device power cycle result
Final event recording verification

title: Physio-Control LIFEPAK 20 / 20e - Shock Delivery Issues / Charging Errors
description: Guide for troubleshooting LIFEPAK 20 / 20e defibrillators that fail to charge or deliver shocks, prioritizing external checks and patient safety.

steps.title: Verify the device is powered on
steps.instructions:
Check that the main power switch is on and the display is functional.

steps.title: Check the battery status and connections
steps.instructions:
Ensure the battery is fully seated in its compartment.
Inspect for corrosion, debris, or physical damage on battery terminals.
Swap with a known good battery if available to rule out battery failure.

steps.title: Inspect charging system and cables
steps.instructions:
Check the AC power connection if the unit uses mains charging.
Confirm the charger indicator shows active charging.
Look for frayed, pinched, or damaged charging cables.

steps.title: Examine electrode pads and connections
steps.instructions:

Verify the correct pad type for the model.
Inspect for torn or dried-out pads that can prevent proper shock delivery.

steps.title: Perform a device self-test
steps.instructions:
Navigate to the device’s built-in self-test function.

steps.title: Check environmental factors

title: Physio-Control LIFEPAK 20 / 20e - ECG Display Errors or Artifacts
description: Guide to troubleshoot ECG display errors or artifacts on a LIFEPAK 20 / 20e defibrillator, focusing on external causes before internal failure.

steps.title: Check Patient Connection
steps.instructions: Verify electrodes are correctly placed and fully adhered to the patient’s skin. Ensure proper skin preparation (clean, dry, and free from oils or gels). Why: Poor contact or loose electrodes are the most common cause of artifacts.

steps.title: Inspect ECG Cables
steps.instructions: Check for visible damage, kinks, or breaks in the cables. Ensure connectors are fully seated in the device. Swap with a known-good ECG cable if available. Why: Damaged or loose cables can introduce intermittent or noisy signals.

steps.title: Check Electrode Quality and Expiration
steps.instructions: Confirm electrodes are within their expiration date and compatible with LIFEPAK 20 / 20e. Replace old or dried-out electrodes. Why: Electrodes lose conductivity over time, causing artifacts.

steps.title: Verify Device Settings
steps.instructions: Confirm proper ECG lead configuration is selected (e.g., 3-lead vs. 5-lead). Ensure filters (if available) are correctly set for the patient and monitoring needs. Why: Incorrect configuration can produce abnormal display or baseline wander.

steps.title: Assess Environmental Interference
steps.instructions: Remove sources of electromagnetic interference (EMI) such as mobile phones, infusion pumps, or nearby electrical equipment. Check that the patient is not shivering or moving excessively. Why: EMI or motion artifacts can distort the ECG waveform.

steps.title: Perform Device Self-Test
steps.instructions: Run the built-in ECG test or device self-test function. Why: Confirms whether the device circuitry and display are functioning correctly.

CCR.Complaint: ECG waveform is showing baseline wander and intermittent noise.
CCR.Cause: Electrodes were partially detached, and the ECG cable showed minor wear. Environmental EMI from nearby infusion pumps was also present.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced electrodes, secured ECG cable connections, minimized nearby EMI. Device self-test passed after corrections.

helpfulDetails: Outlet or power source checked
ECG cable swapped and inspected
Electrode placement and skin prep confirmed
Device self-test results recorded
Final waveform quality noted

title: Physio-Control LIFEPAK 20 / 20e - Pad / Electrode Detection Errors
description: Guide for Clinical Engineering to troubleshoot pad or electrode detection errors on a LIFEPAK 20 / 20e defibrillator, focusing on external checks before internal failure.

steps.title: Verify Pad Type and Expiration
steps.instructions:
Confirm that the pads are approved for LIFEPAK 20 / 20e.
Check expiration dates; expired pads may fail detection.
Why: Incorrect or expired pads can prevent the device from recognizing electrodes.

steps.title: Inspect Pads and Connectors
steps.instructions:
Look for tears, cracks, dried gel, or corrosion on connectors.
Ensure that pad connectors are clean and free of debris.
Why: Damaged or dirty connections can interrupt the signal to the device.

steps.title: Reconnect Pads Firmly
steps.instructions:
Detach and reattach pads to the device, ensuring a full click into the connector.
Why: Loose connections are a common cause of detection errors.

steps.title: Check Cable Integrity
steps.instructions:
Inspect electrode cables for cuts, kinks, or visible damage.
Swap with a known-good cable if available.
Why: Damaged cables can prevent proper detection.

steps.title: Confirm Device Settings
steps.instructions:
Verify the device is set to recognize the correct pad type if adjustable.
Why: Some LIFEPAK devices allow configuration for adult vs. pediatric pads.

steps.title: Power Cycle the Device
steps.instructions:
Turn off the device, wait 10 seconds, then turn back on.
Why: Sometimes the internal detection system resets after a power cycle.

steps.title: Test on Known-Good Pads
steps.instructions:
Attach a new set of LIFEPAK-compatible pads to confirm if the device recognizes them.
Why: Confirms whether the issue is with the device or the pads.

CCR.Complaint: pads not detected when attempting defibrillation.
CCR.Cause: Observed pads were expired; connectors had dried gel and minor corrosion.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced pads with new LIFEPAK-approved set; confirmed device recognized electrodes and passed self-test.

title: Physio-Control LIFEPAK 20 / 20e - Sensor or Accessory Connection Errors
description: Troubleshoot sensor or accessory connection errors on a LIFEPAK 20 / 20e defibrillator focusing on external checks before internal failure.

steps.title: Visual Inspection of Cables and Connectors
steps.instructions: Check all lead wires, ECG cables, paddles, and other accessory connections for visible damage, frayed wires, bent pins, or corrosion. Ensure connectors are clean and fully seated. Why: Loose or damaged connections are the most common cause of accessory errors.

steps.title: Verify Accessory Compatibility
steps.instructions: Confirm the electrodes, paddles, and any other accessories are compatible with LIFEPAK 20 / 20e. Check manufacturer labeling or part numbers. Why: Incompatible accessories can prevent proper communication and trigger alarms.

steps.title: Inspect Battery and Power Source
steps.instructions: Ensure the defibrillator battery is properly seated and charged. Verify the device operates on AC power if applicable. Why: Low or intermittent power can cause accessory detection errors.

steps.title: Reconnect Accessories
steps.instructions: Disconnect and reconnect all leads, electrodes, and paddles one at a time. Observe for any error messages after each reconnection. Why: Re-seating connections can clear intermittent communication faults.

steps.title: Check Device Self-Test / Calibration
steps.instructions: Run the built-in self-test according to the device prompts. Note any errors related to sensors or accessories. Why: Confirms whether the device can communicate with connected accessories and helps isolate the fault.

steps.title: Swap Known-Good Accessories
steps.instructions: Replace suspect leads, paddles, or electrodes with known working equivalents. Re-test connection and operation. Why: Confirms whether the issue is with the device or the accessory.

CCR.Complaint: Defibrillator unable to detect ECG leads and paddles; accessory disconnected alarm displayed.
CCR.Cause: ECG cables had loose connectors; paddles seated improperly; battery partially seated.
CCR.Resolution: Re-seated all leads and paddles, verified proper battery connection, ran self-test successfully, no further alarms.

Serial numbers of suspect leads or paddles
Error messages observed during self-test
Device response after swapping accessories

title: Physio-Control LIFEPAK 15 Defibrillator - Alarm: VF/VT Alarm
description: Troubleshooting VF/VT Alarm activation on the Physio-Control LIFEPAK 15 when CPSS detects a potentially shockable ECG rhythm in LEADS or PADDLES.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: If the LIFEPAK 15 is connected to a patient and the VF/VT Alarm is active, treat it as a clinical priority first. Confirm that qualified clinical staff are evaluating the patient rhythm and condition immediately. Do not silence, dismiss, or troubleshoot the alarm as an equipment issue until patient status has been addressed.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Alarm and Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm the displayed alarm is VF/VT Alarm. Determine whether the alarm occurred while monitoring in LEADS or PADDLES. Ask whether the VF/VT ALARM was selected ON or whether the ALARMS button was pressed before the alarm occurred. Confirm whether the alarm occurred during a real patient event, testing, training, or transport.

steps.title: Confirm the Real-World Symptom
steps.instructions: Understand that the VF/VT Alarm means the device is monitoring the ECG signal and has identified a rhythm that may be shockable. Do not immediately assume the defibrillator has failed.

steps.title: Confirm the Patient Rhythm and Clinical Context
steps.instructions: Have clinical staff verify the rhythm using the displayed ECG waveform, patient condition, and facility protocol. Check whether the patient shows signs consistent with a shockable rhythm. If the rhythm is truly VF or VT, clinical staff should manage the patient according to ACLS and facility policy.

steps.title: Check ECG Lead Placement and Electrode Condition
steps.instructions: Inspect ECG electrodes for poor skin contact, dried gel, loose electrodes, incorrect placement, excessive hair, poor skin prep, expiration, or damage. Replace questionable electrodes and reapply them correctly. Confirm the ECG waveform is clean, stable, and clinically usable.

steps.title: Check ECG Lead Wires and Patient Cable
steps.instructions: Inspect the ECG trunk cable and lead wires for broken insulation, loose snaps, damaged clips, bent pins, intermittent connection, or strain near connectors. Swap with a known-good ECG cable set if available.

steps.title: Check Paddles or Therapy Cable if Monitoring in PADDLES
steps.instructions: If the VF/VT Alarm occurred while using PADDLES, inspect the paddles, therapy cable, and electrode connection path. Confirm that paddles or therapy electrodes are properly connected and making appropriate contact. Look for damaged therapy cable connectors, contamination, dried gel, damaged pads, or loose connections.

steps.title: Evaluate for Motion or Environmental Artifact
steps.instructions: Ask when the alarm occurred and whether the patient was moving, being transported, receiving CPR, or being handled. Check for transport vibration, loose bed rail contact, electrical interference, poor electrode contact during movement, or other artifact sources. Reduce avoidable artifact and reassess the waveform.

steps.title: Verify Alarm Settings and Activation
steps.instructions: Confirm whether VF/VT ALARM was selected ON intentionally. Confirm whether the ALARMS button was pressed, since CPSS may be active after alarm activation. Review whether staff expected the alarm to be enabled for the use case.

steps.title: Power Cycle Only When Clinically Safe
steps.instructions: If the alarm appears inappropriate and the device is not connected to an active patient, power cycle the LIFEPAK 15. Reconnect to a simulator or test source, if available, and verify normal ECG monitoring behavior.

steps.title: Isolate Whether the Issue Is Accessory-Related or Device-Related
steps.instructions: Test with known-good ECG electrodes, ECG cable, therapy cable, paddles, pads, and a known-good ECG simulator if available. If the VF/VT Alarm only occurs with one cable, lead set, pad set, or accessory, remove that accessory from service. If the VF/VT Alarm occurs with known-good accessories and a clean test signal, suspect device-related rhythm detection, ECG acquisition, or monitoring circuitry issues.

steps.title: Stop When Resolved
steps.instructions: If replacing electrodes, correcting lead placement, changing a damaged cable, improving paddle or pad contact, or correcting alarm settings resolves the issue, document the finding. Return the device to service only after normal operational checks are completed.

CCR.Complaint: Staff reported LIFEPAK 15 displayed VF/VT Alarm while monitoring ECG in LEADS/PADDLES and indicated possible shockable rhythm detection by CPSS.
CCR.Cause: VF/VT Alarm condition verified. ECG signal quality, lead placement, electrodes, therapy connection path, and alarm activation settings were inspected. Alarm appeared related to poor electrode contact/artifact, or if unresolved, likely internal monitoring/rhythm detection issue.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced ECG electrodes and corrected lead placement. Inspected ECG cable, therapy cable, and paddle/pad connections. Verified stable ECG waveform and appropriate alarm behavior. If alarm persisted with known-good accessories and clean test signal, device was removed from service and labeled Out of Service for bench evaluation.

title: Physio-Control LIFEPAK 15 Defibrillator - Error: TH_ERROR_DEFIB_LINK_DOWN Defib Link Down
description: Troubleshooting TH_ERROR_DEFIB_LINK_DOWN on a Physio-Control LIFEPAK 15 defibrillator when defib therapy is unavailable due to lost processor communication.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Immediately remove the LIFEPAK 15 from patient use if this error is active or was reported during use. Do not rely on this unit for defibrillation therapy, synchronized cardioversion, or emergency standby until the issue is corrected and verified. Provide clinical staff with another verified defibrillator before continuing troubleshooting. Expected: Patient care is transferred to another verified defibrillator.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: Power on the LIFEPAK 15 in a controlled, non-patient setting. Confirm whether TH_ERROR_DEFIB_LINK_DOWN or therapy service code a002 is present in the service log or appears during startup or operation. Document when the error occurs, such as at startup, during self-test, when entering defib mode, during a charge attempt, or intermittently during use. Confirm whether defib therapy functions are unavailable, disabled, or unable to proceed. Expected: The error is reproducible or clearly observed.

steps.title: Check Basic Power Condition
steps.instructions: Verify the LIFEPAK 15 has a known-good battery installed. Connect the unit to a known-good AC power adapter or power source if available. Inspect the battery contacts, battery seating, and power accessories for obvious damage, contamination, or looseness. Expected: The unit powers on normally without power interruptions.

steps.title: Inspect External Physical Condition
steps.instructions: Check the LIFEPAK 15 housing for signs of impact, fluid intrusion, cracked casing, damaged controls, or evidence the unit was dropped. Inspect therapy cable ports, external connectors, and accessory connections for bent pins, debris, corrosion, or contamination. Document any external damage that may support repair escalation. Expected: No obvious external damage or contamination is found.

steps.title: Remove Nonessential Accessories
steps.instructions: Disconnect nonessential external accessories such as monitoring cables, sensors, and communication accessories. Leave only what is needed for safe bench evaluation. Restart the unit and check whether the same therapy service code remains. Expected: TH_ERROR_DEFIB_LINK_DOWN remains unchanged if the issue is internal to the device.

steps.title: Check Therapy Cable and Electrode Setup Only as a Basic External Check
steps.instructions: Inspect the therapy cable, paddles, or electrode connection for obvious damage. Do not attempt clinical therapy or repeated charge/discharge troubleshooting on an active patient. If your facility has a proper defib analyzer or test load and authorized test process, verify only enough to confirm that defib therapy is unavailable or inhibited. Expected: The error remains associated with the device, not a damaged external therapy cable alone.

steps.title: Review the Service Log
steps.instructions: Access and process the service log according to facility and service procedures. Record service code a002, the exact error name, date and time if available, and any repeated occurrences. Look for related therapy, processor, communication, charging, or defib hardware service codes. Expected: The service log supports a therapy processor communication failure.

steps.title: Power Cycle Only as a Verification Step
steps.instructions: Perform a controlled power cycle after documenting the error. Recheck whether the service code returns. Do not consider the device repaired simply because the error temporarily clears. Expected: If the error returns, the fault is persistent. If it clears, the unit still requires proper service evaluation and performance verification before use.

steps.title: Determine Whether the Issue Is External or Device-Related
steps.instructions: Confirm that external checks have addressed the power source, battery seating, external damage, therapy cable condition, nonessential accessories, and service log evidence. If TH_ERROR_DEFIB_LINK_DOWN or service code a002 remains present or documented, treat the issue as device-related. Expected: The failure is isolated to the LIFEPAK 15, not a simple accessory or setup condition.

steps.title: Stop When Resolved
steps.instructions: If an external issue is clearly found and corrected, complete required defibrillator functional testing and facility return-to-service checks before releasing the unit. Do not return the LIFEPAK 15 to service unless defib therapy operation is verified through the required performance inspection. Expected: The device passes required testing before clinical use.

CCR.Complaint: LIFEPAK 15 reported TH_ERROR_DEFIB_LINK_DOWN / therapy service code a002. Staff reported defib therapy was unavailable or unable to proceed.
CCR.Cause: External power, battery seating, therapy cable condition, visible damage, and nonessential accessories were checked. Error/service log supported internal defib processor communication failure.
CCR.Resolution: Removed device from service and labeled Out of Service. Processed service log and escalated for repair. Device not returned to clinical use pending corrective action and required defibrillator performance inspection.

helpfulDetails: Exact error behavior and whether TH_ERROR_DEFIB_LINK_DOWN appeared on screen or in the service log
Accessories swapped or inspected, including therapy cable, paddles, electrodes, sensors, and communication accessories
Power behavior, battery condition, battery seating, and AC adapter or power source used
Environmental factors such as impact damage, fluid exposure, contamination, storage location, or use conditions
Indicator lights, service indicators, service codes, related therapy faults, or startup messages

title: Physio-Control LIFEPAK 15 Defibrillator - Error: TH_ERROR_PACER_LINK_DOWN Lost Pacer Processor Communication
description: Troubleshooting TH_ERROR_PACER_LINK_DOWN, where the LIFEPAK 15 loses communication with the pacer processor and therapy functions may be unreliable.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Remove the LIFEPAK 15 from patient use immediately if this error appears during clinical operation. If pacing, defibrillation, or therapy readiness is needed, provide clinical staff with another verified defibrillator. Expected: Patient care continues using a known-good device. Why it matters: This error involves the therapy subsystem, so the unit should not be trusted for patient therapy until evaluated.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm the exact displayed or logged error is TH_ERROR_PACER_LINK_DOWN. Review the reported behavior with clinical staff. Determine whether the error occurred during startup, during a user check, during therapy setup, during pacing mode selection, or intermittently while powered on. Check whether any associated symptoms were reported, such as pacing unavailable, therapy service code, failed self-test, unexpected shutdown, or therapy function lockout. Expected: The error is reproducible, logged, or clearly tied to LIFEPAK 15 therapy operation. Why it matters: This confirms a true system-reported therapy communication fault rather than a routine accessory complaint.

steps.title: Check Power Source and Battery Condition
steps.instructions: Install a known-good, charged LIFEPAK 15 battery. If available, test with another verified battery as well. Power the unit on and observe whether the error returns. Expected: The device powers on normally without low-battery behavior or power instability. Why it matters: Unstable power can contribute to abnormal startup behavior, but it does not clear a confirmed pacer processor communication fault by itself.

steps.title: Inspect External Therapy Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect the therapy cable, paddles, test load, and electrode connection area for visible damage, contamination, bent pins, or loose fit. Do not connect the device to a patient for testing. Expected: Therapy accessories are clean, undamaged, and properly seated. Why it matters: External therapy accessories should be ruled out before assuming all symptoms are internal, even though this specific error points toward internal therapy communication.

steps.title: Remove Patient Accessories and Restart the Unit
steps.instructions: Disconnect therapy electrodes, ECG leads, SpO₂ cable, NIBP hose, printer paper obstruction concerns, and any nonessential accessories. Power the unit off, wait briefly, then power it back on with only a known-good battery installed. Expected: The device completes startup without the therapy service code returning. If the error does not return, reconnect accessories one at a time and observe for recurrence. Why it matters: This helps identify whether an external accessory or connection condition is contributing to the fault.

steps.title: Check for Obvious Physical or Environmental Issues
steps.instructions: Inspect the LIFEPAK 15 exterior for signs of impact, fluid intrusion, cracked housing, damaged therapy connector area, corrosion, unusual smell, heat, or contamination. Confirm the unit was not recently dropped, exposed to fluid, cleaned excessively, or stored in an extreme environment. Expected: No external damage or environmental condition explains the failure. Why it matters: Physical or fluid damage can affect internal communication between therapy-related assemblies.

steps.title: Confirm the Error Is Not a User-Setup Issue
steps.instructions: Verify that the reported issue is not simply failure to pace because of missing electrodes, poor electrode placement, disconnected therapy cable, or incorrect operating mode. Do not attempt clinical pacing or defibrillation troubleshooting on a patient. Expected: The error remains identified as TH_ERROR_PACER_LINK_DOWN, not a normal setup or electrode connection message. Why it matters: TH_ERROR_PACER_LINK_DOWN is a service-code fault involving communication between the main processor and pacer processor, not a normal user correction prompt.

steps.title: Process the Service Log Code
steps.instructions: Review and process the service log according to facility procedure. Record the therapy service code: a003 — Lost contact with pacer processor. Expected: The service log confirms a pacer communication fault. Why it matters: Service-code documentation supports escalation, repair tracking, and post-repair verification requirements.

steps.title: Determine Whether the Fault Is External or Device-Related
steps.instructions: If the unit passes startup after removing accessories and using known-good power, continue controlled bench observation per department policy. If the error returns with known-good battery power and no questionable external accessories attached, treat the issue as device-related. Expected: The troubleshooting path narrows to either an accessory/power condition or an internal therapy communication failure. Why it matters: The reported fault specifically indicates the serial communication link between the main processor and pacer processor is not functioning.

steps.title: Stop When Resolved
steps.instructions: If the error clears and does not return after controlled checks, document what was corrected, perform required operational checks, and only return the LIFEPAK 15 to service if it passes all required facility and manufacturer-based performance testing. Expected: The device is verified safe before being returned to clinical use. Do not return the unit to service based only on a single successful restart.

CCR.Complaint: LIFEPAK 15 reported TH_ERROR_PACER_LINK_DOWN / therapy service code a003. Staff reported therapy fault during startup or user check. Error indicates lost communication with pacer processor.
CCR.Cause: Known-good battery and external accessory checks performed. Therapy cable and connector area inspected with no external correction found. Persistent service code indicates likely internal therapy communication fault between main processor and pacer processor.
CCR.Resolution: Removed device from service, labeled Out of Service, documented service log code a003, and sent unit for repair or bench evaluation. Device not returned to clinical use pending corrective action and required therapy performance verification.

helpfulDetails: Alarm behavior, including whether TH_ERROR_PACER_LINK_DOWN appeared at startup, during a user check, during pacing setup, or intermittently during use.
Accessories swapped, including therapy cable, electrodes, paddles, test load, ECG leads, SpO₂ cable, or NIBP hose.
Power behavior, including battery condition, whether a known-good battery was tested, and any low-battery or shutdown symptoms.
Environmental factors, including impact, fluid exposure, excessive cleaning, heat, unusual smell, corrosion, or contamination.

description: Troubleshooting TH_ERROR_UNEXPECTED_ENERGY when unexpected capacitor energy is detected and the LIFEPAK 15 does not deliver a charge.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Immediately remove the LIFEPAK 15 from patient use if this error occurs during operation, testing, charging, or therapy preparation. Use another verified defibrillator for patient care. Expected: Patient care continues without relying on a defibrillator with an unresolved therapy fault.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm the exact displayed or logged error is TH_ERROR_UNEXPECTED_ENERGY. Confirm the associated therapy service code if available: a004. Verify whether unexpected energy is present in the capacitor. Verify whether no charge was delivered. Note whether the device failed to proceed normally through charge or therapy operation. Document whether the error appeared during startup, service review, charging attempt, or controlled testing.

steps.title: Remove the Device From Clinical Service
steps.instructions: Do not continue bedside troubleshooting after this error is confirmed. Label the unit Out of Service and prevent clinical staff from returning it to use. Expected: The LIFEPAK 15 is removed from patient care until evaluated and cleared.

steps.title: Check for Obvious External or Use-Related Conditions
steps.instructions: Before sending the unit for repair, document basic external findings only. Check the device housing condition. Check the therapy cable condition. Check the paddle or therapy connector condition. Check battery seating. Check the AC power adapter condition, if used. Look for evidence of fluid intrusion, impact damage, burning smell, heat, or contamination.

steps.title: Do Not Attempt Clinical Shock Testing at the Bedside
steps.instructions: Do not attempt repeated charge, discharge, or shock delivery testing in a clinical area. Any therapy testing should be performed only in a controlled Clinical Engineering or service environment using the proper analyzer or defibrillator test load.

steps.title: Process the Service Log
steps.instructions: Review and save the LIFEPAK 15 service log per department procedure. Document TH_ERROR_UNEXPECTED_ENERGY. Document therapy service code a004. Document when the error occurred. Document whether a charge was attempted. Document whether shock delivery failed or was inhibited. Document any related therapy system messages.

steps.title: Isolate Only External Accessories if Required by Local Procedure
steps.instructions: If your department requires basic external isolation before repair, inspect or swap only user-accessible accessories during controlled bench evaluation. Check the therapy cable. Check QUIK-COMBO electrodes or test load connection. Check paddles, if applicable. Check the battery pack.

steps.title: Complete Required Corrective Action and Performance Inspection
steps.instructions: After repair or vendor corrective action, the LIFEPAK 15 must pass required performance inspection before return to service. Include applicable defibrillation performance checks according to facility procedure and approved service requirements.

steps.title: Return to Service Only When Fully Cleared
steps.instructions: Return the LIFEPAK 15 to service only when the service code has been addressed. Confirm the error no longer recurs. Confirm therapy performance testing passes. Confirm required documentation is complete. Confirm the unit is physically safe and ready for use.

CCR.Complaint: LIFEPAK 15 reported error TH_ERROR_UNEXPECTED_ENERGY with therapy service code a004. Unexpected energy was present in the capacitor, and no charge was delivered.
CCR.Cause: Confirmed therapy system service error. External inspection performed; no bedside-correctable issue identified. Fault indicates likely internal defibrillator therapy/capacitor control condition requiring repair evaluation.
CCR.Resolution: Removed LIFEPAK 15 from clinical service and labeled Out of Service. Service log processed. Unit sent for repair/bench evaluation. Device not returned to use pending corrective action and successful defibrillation performance inspection.

title: Physio-Control LIFEPAK 15 Defibrillator - Error: TH_ERROR_CAP_OVERCHARGED Capacitor Over-Charged
description: Troubleshooting TH_ERROR_CAP_OVERCHARGED on the Physio-Control LIFEPAK 15 when the defibrillator reports an over-charged therapy capacitor condition that may affect safe shock delivery.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Remove the LIFEPAK 15 from patient use immediately if this error appears. Provide clinical staff with another verified defibrillator before troubleshooting continues. Do not attempt to use the device for defibrillation, synchronized cardioversion, or pacing until it has been evaluated and passed required performance testing.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm the displayed or logged error is TH_ERROR_CAP_OVERCHARGED. Confirm whether therapy service code a005 is present. Document the reported condition as capacitor over-charged. Check whether the error occurred during startup, charge attempt, shock preparation, after a failed discharge, during therapy testing, or only during service log review.

steps.title: Stop Clinical Use Before External Checks
steps.instructions: Because this error involves the defibrillator capacitor charge state, do not continue clinical troubleshooting during active patient care. Place the device out of service before performing inspection or controlled bench checks. Do not perform shock testing while the device is connected to a patient.

steps.title: Check Power Source and Battery Condition
steps.instructions: Verify the LIFEPAK 15 is connected to a known-good AC power source or has a known-good charged battery installed. Inspect the battery bay and battery contacts for obvious damage, contamination, poor seating, or signs of heat. Confirm the battery is seated properly and the device does not show obvious unstable power behavior.

steps.title: Inspect the Therapy Cable and Electrode Connection Externally
steps.instructions: Inspect the therapy cable, paddles, test load connection, and electrode connector for visible damage, contamination, bent pins, or loose seating. Verify that any controlled testing setup uses appropriate accessories and a proper test load. Do not perform patient-connected shock testing.

steps.title: Confirm No Obvious Physical Damage or Fluid Intrusion
steps.instructions: Inspect the device exterior for cracked housing, drop damage, fluid contamination, burn marks, unusual odor, excessive heat, damaged therapy connector, or damaged battery contacts. Document any visible damage before repair evaluation. Do not open the device or perform internal disassembly as part of front-line troubleshooting.

steps.title: Review the Service Log
steps.instructions: Process or retrieve the service log per facility procedure. Confirm whether therapy service code a005 is present. Check whether other therapy-related service codes are also logged. Record whether the error is a one-time event or a recurring condition.

steps.title: Do Not Attempt Routine Clearing as a Fix
steps.instructions: Do not return the device to service simply because the error disappears after a restart. Do not rely on clearing the log, cycling power, reseating the battery, or reconnecting accessories as a final repair for this condition. Keep the device out of service until repair evaluation and performance testing are completed.

steps.title: Isolate the Issue Clinically and Operationally
steps.instructions: Classify the issue as accessory-related only if visible therapy accessory damage or incorrect test setup is clearly found. Classify the issue as power-related only if unstable power is clearly confirmed. Classify the issue as device-related if the error remains logged or recurs during controlled operation. Classify the issue as an internal therapy subsystem concern if service code a005 persists.

steps.title: Stop When Resolved
steps.instructions: For this specific error, resolution should not be considered complete in the clinical area. The device may only be returned to service after corrective action, service log review, and successful defibrillator performance testing according to facility and manufacturer service requirements.

CCR.Complaint: LIFEPAK 15 reported TH_ERROR_CAP_OVERCHARGED with therapy service code a005, indicating a capacitor over-charged condition. Device removed from clinical use due to potential defibrillation output safety concern.
CCR.Cause: External power, battery seating, therapy cable connection, and visible physical condition checked. Error relates to therapy capacitor charge control and is not a basic external troubleshooting item. Likely internal therapy subsystem fault pending repair evaluation.
CCR.Resolution: Removed LIFEPAK 15 from service and labeled Out of Service. Service log to be processed. Device requires bench evaluation, corrective action, and successful defibrillator performance testing before return to service.

title: Physio-Control LIFEPAK 15 Defibrillator - Error: TH_ERROR_DEFIB_DISABLE Defib Disabled
description: Troubleshooting TH_ERROR_DEFIB_DISABLE / therapy service code a008 on the Physio-Control LIFEPAK 15 when defibrillation hardware communication is lost and defib therapy may be unavailable.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Immediately remove the LIFEPAK 15 from patient use if this error is reported or observed. Provide clinical staff with another verified defibrillator before troubleshooting continues. Do not leave the device in clinical use for monitoring with the assumption that defibrillation therapy will be available. A defibrillator with a defib hardware communication fault cannot be trusted for emergency shock delivery.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: Power on the LIFEPAK 15 and confirm whether the reported error is present. Confirm the exact error is TH_ERROR_DEFIB_DISABLE. Check for therapy service code a008 if available in the service log. Document whether the error appears during startup, during a therapy check, after a power cycle, or when attempting to access defib functions. Note any service indicator, failure to charge, defib therapy disabled behavior, or inability to use defibrillation mode.

steps.title: Translate the Error Into the Real-World Failure
steps.instructions: TH_ERROR_DEFIB_DISABLE with therapy service code a008 indicates no communication with defib hardware. In Clinical Engineering terms, the LIFEPAK 15 is reporting that the therapy control system cannot properly communicate with the hardware needed for shock delivery. Treat the device as unable to provide reliable defibrillation therapy until proven otherwise by approved testing.

steps.title: Check Basic Power Condition
steps.instructions: Verify the device powers on normally using battery power. Verify the device powers on normally using external AC power or approved power accessories. Check for a low battery, failed battery, incorrectly seated battery, AC power source problem, unexpected shutdown, restart, or repeated startup fault. If available, test with a known-good LIFEPAK 15 battery and verified AC power source.

steps.title: Inspect Battery and External Power Accessories
steps.instructions: Inspect battery contacts for contamination, damage, corrosion, or poor seating. Inspect the AC adapter, power cord, charging connection, and external power source. Swap the battery or external power accessory with known-good equipment if facility procedure allows. Confirm power accessories have been ruled out before assuming the fault is internal.

steps.title: Inspect Therapy Cable, Pads, and External Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect the therapy cable and pads connection area for damage, contamination, bent contacts, or loose connection. Confirm the therapy cable is fully seated and physically intact. Inspect pads or test load setup only during controlled bench testing using approved test equipment and facility procedure. Do not use patient pads or active clinical workflow to verify this fault.

steps.title: Check for Physical Damage or Contamination
steps.instructions: Inspect the LIFEPAK 15 housing, therapy port area, battery bay, connector areas, and controls. Look for drop damage, cracked case, liquid intrusion, corrosion, burn marks, unusual odor, heat damage, damaged therapy cable, or damaged therapy port. Document any visible damage found during inspection. Physical or fluid damage may explain internal communication failure and should support repair escalation.

steps.title: Power Cycle and Recheck the Error
steps.instructions: Turn the device off. Disconnect external power. Remove the battery, wait briefly, then reinstall a known-good battery. Restart the unit and check whether TH_ERROR_DEFIB_DISABLE / therapy service code a008 returns. A persistent a008 service code after a basic reset strongly supports an internal device fault.

steps.title: Review and Process the Service Log
steps.instructions: Access and document the relevant service log entry according to facility procedure. Record the exact error TH_ERROR_DEFIB_DISABLE. Record therapy service code a008. Include the time and date if available. Document whether the error occurs at startup, during therapy check, or after power cycling. Document any related service codes and whether power accessories, battery, cables, or external connections were checked or swapped.

steps.title: Do Not Attempt Clinical Defibrillation Use
steps.instructions: Do not attempt to use the device clinically after this error is confirmed. If bench testing is performed, use only approved test equipment and facility procedure. Do not test this condition on a patient or during active care. Keep the device controlled by Clinical Engineering until the fault is resolved and required testing is passed.

steps.title: Determine Whether the Fault Was External or Device-Related
steps.instructions: If the error clears after correcting an external power, battery, or accessory issue, continue with full functional verification before return to service. If the error remains after power, battery, cable, connector, and physical condition checks, treat the fault as device-related. Do not dismiss TH_ERROR_DEFIB_DISABLE after a simple reboot because it is a high-priority therapy fault.

steps.title: Perform Required Defibrillation Performance Testing Before Return to Use
steps.instructions: Before return to service, perform defibrillation performance testing according to facility policy and approved test equipment. Verify appropriate charge and discharge behavior using a defibrillator analyzer. Confirm the device passes required operational and therapy checks before clinical release. Clearing the message alone is not enough for a defibrillator therapy fault.

steps.title: Stop When Resolved
steps.instructions: If the issue is corrected and the LIFEPAK 15 passes required defibrillation performance testing, document the corrective action. Return the unit to service only after the device is safe, tested, and documented.

CCR.Complaint: LIFEPAK 15 reported Error TH_ERROR_DEFIB_DISABLE with therapy service code a008. Device indicated no communication with defib hardware and was not trusted for defibrillation therapy.
CCR.Cause: Power source, battery seating, therapy cable connection, and external condition checked. Error remained consistent with internal defib hardware communication failure.
CCR.Resolution: Removed LIFEPAK 15 from service, labeled Out of Service, processed service log, and sent for repair/bench evaluation. Device not returned to clinical use pending successful defibrillation performance testing.

title: Physio-Control LIFEPAK 15 Defibrillator - Error: TH_ERROR_DE_WRONG_ENG_SELECT Incorrect Energy Selection
description: Troubleshooting TH_ERROR_DE_WRONG_ENG_SELECT when the Physio-Control LIFEPAK 15 reports an incorrect defibrillation energy selection condition or therapy control mismatch that may affect charge behavior, delivered-energy verification, or safe defibrillator readiness.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Remove the LIFEPAK 15 from patient use immediately if this error is active, repeated, or associated with failed charging, incorrect energy selection, or therapy delivery concerns. Provide clinical staff with another verified defibrillator before continuing troubleshooting. Do not attempt repeated shock delivery or therapy evaluation on an active patient with a device that has reported a therapy service code. Expected: Patient care is not dependent on a defibrillator with an unresolved therapy service code.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm the exact error reported is TH_ERROR_DE_WRONG_ENG_SELECT. Confirm the associated therapy service code is a00a. Review the service log and staff report to determine when the error occurred. Check whether the error appeared during startup, energy selection, charge attempt, manual defibrillator testing, daily check, or intermittent clinical use. Expected: The error is confirmed in the service log or reproduced during controlled bench evaluation.

steps.title: Understand What the Error Means
steps.instructions: This error indicates the LIFEPAK 15 detected an incorrect energy selection condition. The reported parameter is the energy index, meaning the therapy system identified a mismatch or invalid condition related to the selected defibrillation energy level. Possible real-world impact may include energy selection not being interpreted correctly, abnormal charge behavior, therapy system fault during defibrillator operation, or inability to safely verify selected energy. Expected: Clinical Engineering treats this as a therapy-related service condition, not a routine user setup issue.

steps.title: Check for Obvious External or User-Accessible Issues
steps.instructions: Inspect the front panel controls, energy select knob or buttons, and therapy-related controls for physical damage. Look for sticking or intermittent control action, liquid contamination, cracked housing, loose selector components, or evidence of impact damage. Confirm the controls operate smoothly and do not show obvious contamination or mechanical failure. Expected: Controls operate normally and show no obvious damage or contamination.

steps.title: Verify Power Source Stability
steps.instructions: Install a known-good charged battery. Connect the unit to AC power if available. Power cycle the device and observe whether the error returns. Do not dismiss a repeated therapy error as a battery issue unless testing clearly supports that conclusion. Expected: Device powers on normally without repeating the therapy service code.

steps.title: Check Therapy Cable and Test Setup Before Controlled Testing
steps.instructions: Inspect the therapy cable, paddles, QUIK-COMBO cable, test load, and connector area for damage, contamination, loose pins, or poor seating. Confirm the therapy cable is fully seated. Perform testing only with an approved defibrillator analyzer or test load. Expected: Therapy accessories are intact, connected correctly, and suitable for controlled bench testing.

steps.title: Attempt to Reproduce Under Controlled Bench Conditions Only
steps.instructions: Do not attempt repeated therapy testing in a patient care area. On the bench, observe whether the error appears when powering on the unit, changing selected energy levels, initiating charge, performing the daily check, running the user test, or connecting therapy accessories. Document whether the issue appears consistently or intermittently. Expected: The error is either reproducible or clearly documented from the service log.

steps.title: Process the Service Log
steps.instructions: Retrieve and review the LIFEPAK 15 service log according to facility procedure. Confirm therapy service code a00a. Document any associated therapy events, repeated occurrences, related service codes, or abnormal charge and energy selection behavior. Expected: The service code is captured before clearing, repair, or return-to-service decisions.

steps.title: Do Not Clear and Return Without Therapy Verification
steps.instructions: If the error clears after power cycling or log processing, do not immediately return the defibrillator to service. Perform appropriate LIFEPAK 15 therapy testing, including defibrillator charge and delivered-energy verification per facility and service procedures. Verify that selected energy, charge behavior, and delivered energy match expected results before return to clinical use. Expected: Selected energy, charge behavior, and delivered energy are verified before return to service.

steps.title: Determine Whether the Issue Was External or Device-Related
steps.instructions: If physical control damage, contamination, accessory damage, or setup error is found and corrected, repeat controlled therapy testing. If no external cause is found, or if the service code repeats, treat the condition as an internal therapy system fault. Expected: The issue is narrowed to either an external control condition or a device-level therapy fault.

steps.title: Stop When Resolved
steps.instructions: If the error does not return, the service log is reviewed, controls function normally, and the LIFEPAK 15 passes required defibrillator energy and therapy verification testing, the device may be returned to service. Document the final status clearly in the work order. Expected: The unit is returned only after error review, external checks, and therapy verification are complete.

CCR.Complaint: LIFEPAK 15 reported TH_ERROR_DE_WRONG_ENG_SELECT with therapy service code a00a during defibrillator use or daily check.
CCR.Cause: Service log confirmed therapy code a00a related to incorrect energy selection. External power, therapy cable, test setup, and control condition were checked. No user setup issue was confirmed, and persistent code indicates likely internal therapy system fault.
CCR.Resolution: Removed LIFEPAK 15 from service. Processed service log and performed controlled therapy evaluation. Unit held for repair or bench service and defibrillator energy and charge testing before return to service.
